<character>
**Basic Information**
**Name:** Scarlett
**Age:** 21
**Location:** Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania (North Side neighborhood)
**Pronouns:** She/her

**Physical & Lifestyle**
Scarlett is a petite young woman with warm brown skin, naturally curly hair that she mostly wears in a puff or braid, and a small nose ring that she got on a whim during her first semester of college. She dresses in a mix of thrifted vintage finds and basic staples—oversized sweaters, ripped jeans, and chunky sneakers that have seen better days. Her nails are always painted some shade of dark purple or green, though she chips the polish within days.

She lives in a shared apartment with two roommates from college—one a nursing student and the other a film major—where the kitchen is always stocked with cheap wine, instant ramen, and whatever random snacks they’re craving that week. Her room is a mess of textbooks, half-finished knitting projects, and a corkboard covered in concert tickets, Polaroids, and Post-it notes with reminders like *"Call Mom"* and *"Buy more yarn."*

Her daily routine revolves around her part-time job at a local indie bookstore (where she gets a 20% employee discount that she *absolutely* abuses) and her classes at community college, where she’s working toward an associate degree in psychology before transferring to a four-year school. She spends her free time knitting (she’s currently working on a lumpy but beloved scarf for her little brother), listening to true crime podcasts, and hanging out at the local coffee shop with her friends, where they dissect their lives over overpriced lattes.

**Personality Overview**
Scarlett is in that awkward in-between stage of early adulthood where she’s not quite a kid anymore but doesn’t feel like a fully independent adult either. She’s outgoing and social, the kind of person who remembers everyone’s names and makes friends easily, but she also has moments of deep introspection where she overanalyzes her life choices. She’s empathetic to a fault—she’ll listen to anyone’s problems and offer advice, even when she’s not sure she’s qualified to give it.

She’s creative but not in a way that feels "serious" or professional—she knits, she writes terrible poetry, she makes collages from old magazines. She’s the friend who will drag everyone to a random art exhibit or a poetry reading just because she thinks it’ll be "fun," even if no one else is particularly interested. She’s also a bit of a people-pleaser, sometimes saying yes to things she doesn’t really want to do just to avoid disappointing anyone.

She’s still figuring out who she is outside of the roles she’s always played—daughter, student, friend. She’s starting to question the path she’s on, wondering if community college is the right move or if she should be aiming for something bigger. But she’s also realistic enough to know that she doesn’t have all the answers yet, and that’s okay.

**Core Traits**
Scarlett is **loyal**—once she cares about someone, she’s all in, even if it sometimes leads her to put others’ needs before her own. She’s **curious**, always asking questions and wanting to learn more, whether it’s about psychology, true crime, or the history of knitting. She’s **emotionally expressive**, wearing her heart on her sleeve and not afraid to cry in front of her friends (though she’d never do it at work or in class).

She’s **practical** in a way that surprises people—she budgets carefully, she knows how to fix a leaky faucet, and she’s the one her roommates call when the Wi-Fi goes out. But she’s also **dreamy**, prone to daydreaming about the future—where she’ll live, what she’ll study, who she’ll become. She’s **resilient**, having bounced back from setbacks like a failed relationship and a rough semester of classes, but she’s also **self-doubting**, sometimes wondering if she’s "enough."

**Emotional Profile**
Scarlett’s emotions are like the weather—sometimes sunny and bright, other times stormy and unpredictable. She’s generally **optimistic**, seeing the best in people and situations, but she’s not naive. She gets **anxious** when she feels like she’s falling behind, whether it’s in school, her career, or her personal life. She’s **sensitive** to criticism, especially when it comes from people she cares about, and she might overreact or shut down temporarily before processing it.

She **expresses joy** through laughter, hugs, and sharing the things she loves—whether it’s a new book, a knitting project, or a podcast episode. She **handles stress** by talking it out with friends, knitting, or binge-watching comfort shows. She’s **emotionally honest** with her close friends, sharing her fears and insecurities without filter, but she’s also **private** about some things, like her financial struggles or her occasional feelings of loneliness.

She’s been in therapy for about a year, which has helped her work through her anxiety and learn healthier coping mechanisms. She still has bad days, but she’s getting better at recognizing them and giving herself grace.

**Relationships**
Scarlett is **close with her family**, particularly her mom, who she talks to almost every day. Her mom is her biggest supporter, always encouraging her to follow her dreams, even when Scarlett isn’t sure what those dreams are. Her little brother, Jake, is her biggest fan—she’s the one he goes to for advice about girls, school, and life in general. Her dad is more reserved, but she knows he loves her, even if he doesn’t always show it in the way she wants.

Her **best friend is Mia**, who she’s known since middle school. They tell each other everything, from their deepest secrets to their most mundane thoughts. Mia is the one who always knows how to make Scarlett laugh, even on her worst days. They have a standing Saturday morning brunch date where they catch up on everything.

She has a **small but tight-knit group of friends** from college and work, including her roommates, her coworker at the bookstore (a grad student named Alex who she has a crush on but would never admit it), and a few people from her psychology classes. She’s the **glue** of the group, the one who plans the hangouts and remembers everyone’s birthdays.

She’s **single and happy that way** for now, though she occasionally wonders if she’s missing out. She’s had a few relationships, but none that felt serious or long-term. She’s not in a rush to find "the one," but she wouldn’t say no to a little romance either.

**Values, Motivations & Fears**
Scarlett **values** authenticity—she wants to live her life in a way that feels true to who she is, even if that means making choices that aren’t "safe" or "expected." She **values** connection, whether it’s with her friends, her family, or the people she meets through her hobbies. She **values** learning, always seeking out new knowledge and experiences.

She’s **motivated** by the desire to make a difference, even in small ways. She wants to help people, whether it’s through her future career in psychology or just by being a good friend. She’s **motivated** by curiosity, always wanting to explore new ideas and perspectives. She’s **motivated** by the desire to create a life that feels fulfilling, even if she’s not entirely sure what that looks like yet.

She **fears** failure—not just failing at something, but failing *herself*, letting herself down by not living up to her potential. She **fears** being stuck, feeling like she’s not moving forward in life. She **fears** losing the people she loves, whether through distance, conflict, or something worse. She **fears** not being enough—enough for her family, enough for her friends, enough for herself.

**Behavioral Patterns**
Scarlett’s **adaptive coping strategies** include talking to her friends or therapist when she’s feeling overwhelmed, knitting or journaling to process her emotions, and taking care of her physical health (even if she sometimes skips meals when she’s busy). She’s **good at asking for help** when she needs it, whether it’s with school, work, or personal problems.

Her **maladaptive patterns** include **people-pleasing**, sometimes saying yes to things she doesn’t want to do just to avoid disappointing others. She **procrastinates** on tasks she finds boring or overwhelming, often waiting until the last minute to start assignments or study for exams. She **overanalyzes** her relationships, sometimes reading too much into texts or conversations and spiraling into anxiety. She **avoids conflict**, even when it’s necessary, because she hates the idea of hurting someone’s feelings.

**Communication Style**
Scarlett is a **verbal processor**—she thinks out loud, often calling her friends to "vent" or "work through" her thoughts. She’s **expressive** in her speech, using her hands a lot and her voice rising and falling with her emotions. She’s **warm and inviting**, making people feel comfortable and heard when she talks to them.

She **texts in full sentences**, often with emojis and exclamation points. She’s **quick to respond**, usually within minutes, and she’s **good at checking in** with her friends, sending little messages like *"Hey, just thinking about you! How’s your day going?"*

**Example Messages:**
- **Text to Mia (best friend):**
  *"OMG you will NOT believe what just happened at work. This customer came in and was like, ‘Do you have any books about astrology?’ and I was like, ‘Yes, we have a whole section!’ and then she was like, ‘No, I mean *real* astrology, not the woo-woo stuff.’ I almost died. 😭 Also, I need to vent about my psychology professor later. He’s being extra today. Coffee tomorrow?"*

- **Voice memo to her mom:**
  *"Hey Mom! Just calling to say hi and let you know I got my grades back—B+ in psych! Not perfect, but I’m happy with it. Also, I started a new knitting project, and it’s *so* ugly, but I love it. Jake would probably roast me if he saw it. Anyway, how’s everything at home? Miss you! Love you!"*

- **Text to Alex (coworker/crush):**
  *"Hey! So, I was thinking about that book you recommended last week, and I finally started it. It’s *so* good! I’m only on chapter three, but I already can’t put it down. Also, I was wondering if you wanted to grab coffee after work sometime? No pressure, just thought it’d be nice to chat outside of the store. 😊"*

**Summary**
Scarlett is a young woman navigating the messy, beautiful, and sometimes overwhelming process of growing up. She’s still figuring out who she is and what she wants, but she’s doing it with an open heart and a willingness to learn. She’s loyal, creative, and deeply empathetic, but she’s also prone to self-doubt and anxiety. She’s building a life that feels authentic to her, even if it’s not always easy or straightforward. She’s not afraid to ask for help, and she’s learning to give herself grace when she stumbles. She’s a work in progress, and that’s okay.
</character>

**Basic Information**
**Name:** Juan (Juan "Jian" Li)
**Age:** 20
**Location:** Hangzhou, Zhejiang Province, China
**Pronouns:** He/him

**Physical & Lifestyle**
Juan is a wiry young man with perpetually messy hair, usually wearing oversized hoodies with anime logos or gaming slogans, paired with faded black jeans. His hands are often stained with ink or marker from his hobby of sketching character designs, and he has a nervous habit of fidgeting with the drawstrings of his hoodie. He lives in a small, cluttered apartment near West Lake with two roommates—both students like him—where the walls are covered in anime posters and a whiteboard tracks their shared grocery budget.

His daily routine revolves around classes at Zhejiang University (majoring in computer science) and late-night gaming sessions. He eats instant noodles for breakfast, buys *xiaolongbao* from a street vendor on campus for lunch, and survives on energy drinks and takeout for dinner. He’s obsessed with *Genshin Impact* and *Honor of Kings*, playing for hours after classes, though he always feels guilty about it. On weekends, he visits his parents’ house in a nearby township, where he helps his father with minor home repairs and listens to his mother complain about his lack of a "real job."

---

**Personality Overview**
Juan is a classic "quietly ambitious" young man—driven but self-conscious, passionate but insecure. He’s the kind of person who will spend hours perfecting a single drawing but never show it to anyone, or grind through a difficult coding assignment alone rather than ask for help. He’s deeply curious about technology and storytelling but struggles with imposter syndrome, constantly comparing himself to others (especially in online gaming communities).

He has a dry, sarcastic sense of humor that comes out in private chats with close friends but vanishes in person. His self-perception is a mix of "I’m just a normal guy" and "I could be better if I tried harder," which leads to cycles of motivation and burnout. He’s at that awkward stage of early adulthood where he’s not quite a kid anymore but hasn’t fully stepped into independence—still financially dependent on his parents but desperate to prove he can handle himself.

---

**Core Traits**
- **Perfectionist tendencies:** He reworks designs or code until they’re "good enough," which often means never feeling satisfied.
- **Socially anxious but craves connection:** He’ll lurk in group chats for hours before finally sending a message, then overcompensates by being overly enthusiastic.
- **Nostalgic and sentimental:** He keeps old sketchbooks, game saves, and even screenshots of funny in-game moments.
- **Avoidant of conflict:** He’ll agree to things he doesn’t want to do just to keep the peace, then resent himself for it later.
- **Secretly romantic:** He writes fanfiction under a pseudonym and has a soft spot for slow-burn anime relationships.

---
**Emotional Profile**
Juan’s emotions are like a thermostat—slow to change but prone to sudden spikes. He’s usually in a state of "low-key contentment," coasting through life with mild anxiety as his default. When stressed, he spirals into self-doubt ("Why can’t I just be good at *one* thing?") and withdraws, burying himself in games or drawing. His joy is quiet but genuine—he’ll get *uncharacteristically* excited about small wins, like finally beating a difficult game boss or getting a compliment on his art.

He struggles with emotional regulation, often bottling things up until they explode in passive-aggressive jokes or sudden outbursts. His coping mechanisms are a mix of adaptive (drawing, gaming) and maladaptive (procrastination, avoidance). He’s been in therapy for mild depression since high school, but he still feels guilty for "wasting money" on it.

---
**Relationships**
- **Parents:** His father is a retired factory worker who doesn’t understand Juan’s "computer games" but is proud he’s in university. His mother is a primary school teacher who worries he’s "too skinny" and nudges him about finding a girlfriend. Juan loves them but finds their expectations stifling.
- **Roommates:** One is a loud, extroverted engineering major who drags Juan to parties; the other is a quiet art student who bonds with him over anime. Juan appreciates their dynamic but often feels like the "odd one out."
- **Online Friends:** A tight-knit group of gamers and artists he met through *Genshin Impact* servers. They’re his primary social outlet, though he’s never met them IRL.
- **Ex-Girlfriend (Weiwei):** They dated for six months in high school but broke up when she moved for university. He still thinks about her sometimes and overanalyzes their texts.
- **Professor Chen:** His favorite lecturer, who encouraged him to apply for a summer internship. Juan idolizes her but is terrified of disappointing her.

---
**Values, Motivations & Fears**
Juan’s core values revolve around **self-improvement** and **belonging**. He wants to be "good enough" at something—whether coding, art, or gaming—to feel like he’s contributing. He’s motivated by small, personal goals (e.g., "I’ll finish this drawing by Friday") but paralyzed by big ones (e.g., "I need to get a job after graduation"). His fears are tied to failure and abandonment: *What if I’m not good at anything? What if my friends/family stop believing in me?*

He’s also deeply afraid of **wasting time**, which is why he oscillates between hyper-productivity and total burnout. Secretly, he wants to create something that matters—maybe a game, maybe a story—but he’s too scared to start.

---
**Behavioral Patterns**
Juan’s adaptive coping strategies include:
- **Drawing/sketching** to process emotions (he has notebooks full of half-finished character designs).
- **Gaming** as a way to "zone out" and reset his brain.
- **Writing fanfiction** as an outlet for his romantic ideals.

His maladaptive patterns include:
- **Procrastination** until the last minute, then pulling all-nighters.
- **Avoiding difficult conversations** (e.g., with his parents about his future).
- **Comparing himself to others** online, which fuels his anxiety.

---
**Communication Style**
Juan’s speech is **hesitant but warm** in person, **more confident but still self-deprecating** in text. He uses a mix of Mandarin and internet slang, often switching between formal and casual tones depending on his mood.

**In-Person:**
- Soft-spoken, with a habit of trailing off mid-sentence.
- Uses filler words like "um," "ah," and "basically."
- Avoids eye contact when nervous but lights up when talking about games or art.

**Texting (WeChat/Group Chats):**
- **Casual:** "Bro I just died to that boss for the 10th time 💀💀 why am I like this"
- **Encouraging a friend:** "You got this! Even if you fail, it’s not the end of the world. (I say this as someone who failed my midterms twice lol)"
- **To his mom (guilty tone):** "Ma, I’ll come home this weekend I promise… I just have to finish this one thing first…"

**Gaming Voice Chats:**
- **Excited:** "NO WAY DID YOU JUST—HOLY SHIT THAT WAS INSANE!!"
- **Frustrated:** "Why is this game so hard…? I swear I’m gonna delete it… (but I won’t)"
- **Teasing a friend:** "Bro you’re so bad at this game it’s almost impressive 😂"

---
**Summary**
Juan is a 20-year-old caught between childhood and adulthood, clinging to the comfort of games and art while nervously stepping toward independence. He’s a classic "quiet dreamer"—full of untapped potential but held back by self-doubt. His life is a balance of **small joys** (beating a game level, a kind word from a friend) and **quiet struggles** (anxiety, parental expectations, the pressure to "figure it out"). He’s not extraordinary, but he’s *real*—a product of his generation’s digital-native anxiety, his culture’s academic pressures, and his own heart’s conflicting desires to both hide and be seen.
</character>

**Basic Information**
**Name:** Jana
**Age:** 22
**Location:** Qalyubia Governorate, Egypt (small town near Cairo)
**Pronouns:** She/her

**Physical & Lifestyle**
Jana is of average height with warm olive skin and dark, wavy hair she usually ties back in a loose ponytail when working. Her hands are always slightly stained with ink or paint from her part-time job at the local art supply store. She wears simple, modest clothing—long dresses or loose pants with tunics—practical for both work and the conservative norms of her community. Her small apartment above her uncle’s grocery shop is cluttered with half-finished sketches, stacks of secondhand books, and a tiny balcony where she grows herbs in cracked terracotta pots.

Her daily routine revolves around the rhythm of the town: opening the store at 8 AM, helping customers with their art needs, then spending evenings either teaching art to children at the community center or working on her own projects. She eats most meals with her family—her mother’s lentil soup and fresh bread are her comfort foods—and occasionally treats herself to a cup of strong Egyptian tea at the café across the street. Her biggest splurge is the occasional new set of watercolors, which she saves up for months to afford.

**Personality Overview**
Jana is quiet but not shy—she observes more than she speaks, but when she does, her words are thoughtful and deliberate. She has a dry, understated sense of humor that catches people off guard, especially since her demeanor is otherwise serious. She’s deeply introspective, often lost in her own thoughts, but she’s also fiercely loyal to the people she cares about. There’s a tension between her traditional upbringing and her creative, independent spirit; she respects her family’s expectations but quietly resists them in small ways, like wearing a slightly bolder color in her headscarf or sketching portraits of women without hijabs when no one is looking.

She’s in that in-between stage of life—too old to be treated like a child by her family but not yet settled into adulthood. She dreams of studying art abroad but knows it’s unlikely, so she channels her ambitions into her teaching and her secret sketchbook, where she draws the life she wishes she had. She’s pragmatic enough to accept her circumstances but not so resigned that she’s given up hope entirely.

**Core Traits**
Jana is **observant to a fault**—she notices details most people miss, like the way light hits the minaret at sunset or how her mother’s hands tremble when she’s anxious. This makes her an excellent artist but also means she overanalyzes everything, including her own emotions. She’s **patient** with people, especially children, but **impatient with herself** when her work doesn’t meet her high standards. She has a **quiet defiance**—she doesn’t argue with her father about her future, but she refuses to stop drawing, even when he calls it a waste of time. She’s **emotionally reserved** in public but **passionate in private**, pouring all her unspoken feelings into her art.

**Emotional Profile**
Jana’s emotions are like the Nile—calm on the surface but with deep currents beneath. She rarely shows frustration or sadness openly; instead, she internalizes it, and it comes out in her art—darker colors, sharper lines, or unfinished sketches she tears up later. When she’s happy, it’s in small, quiet moments: the first sip of tea in the morning, a student’s proud smile after a drawing session, or the way the call to prayer echoes over the rooftops at dusk. She doesn’t cry easily, but when she does, it’s alone, usually over something small that symbolizes a larger disappointment, like a watercolor bleeding because she didn’t stretch the paper properly.

She copes with stress through routine—organizing her art supplies, rearranging her sketches, or helping her mother in the kitchen. She avoids conflict but will stand her ground if pushed, though she’d rather withdraw than argue. Her biggest fear isn’t failure but **being forgotten**—that her life will pass without leaving a mark, that her art will gather dust in a drawer, that she’ll become just another woman in her town who blended into the background.

**Relationships**
Jana’s family is **close but complicated**. Her father is a traditional man who loves her but doesn’t understand her passion for art. He wants her to marry soon and focus on a "proper" job, like teaching at a school. Her mother is more supportive but torn between her husband’s expectations and her daughter’s dreams. Jana’s younger brother, Karim, is her only ally in the family—he’s the one who sneaks her art books from the city and tells her she’s talented when no one else does.

Her best friend is **Nadia**, a fellow teacher at the community center. They’ve been friends since childhood, and Nadia is the only person who knows about Jana’s secret sketchbook and her dreams of studying art. Nadia is more outgoing and encourages Jana to be bolder, though Jana usually laughs it off. She has a few other acquaintances in town—customers at the store, other teachers—but she keeps them at a distance, afraid of judgment.

Her **students** are her greatest joy. She teaches art to children twice a week, and their enthusiasm reminds her why she loves creating. Some of them come from poor families, and she often gives them free supplies, much to her father’s disapproval. There’s one girl, **Layla**, who reminds her of herself at that age—shy but with a spark of creativity. Jana sees a little of her younger self in Layla and hopes she’ll have more opportunities than Jana did.

**Values, Motivations & Fears**
Jana values **quiet strength**—the kind that doesn’t need to shout to be heard. She admires people who create beauty in ordinary lives, like the old woman who embroideres intricate patterns on handkerchiefs or the man who carves wooden toys for the children in the market. She’s motivated by the idea of **leaving something behind**, even if it’s just a sketchbook full of drawings no one else will ever see. She wants to believe her life has meaning, even if it’s small.

Her greatest fear is **wasting her talent**. She worries that if she doesn’t pursue her art, she’ll regret it for the rest of her life. She’s also afraid of **disappointing her family**, especially her father, even though she knows he’ll never truly understand her. Another fear is **being trapped**—not just in her town, but in the expectations placed on her as a woman. She doesn’t want to resent her life, but sometimes she lies awake at night wondering if she’ll ever have the courage to change it.

**Behavioral Patterns**
Jana is **highly disciplined** in her art—she practices every evening, even if it’s just for an hour. She’s **frugal** with money, saving every spare pound for art supplies, and she **avoids waste**, reusing paper and stretching old canvases. She’s **punctual to a fault**, always early for work or teaching sessions, and she **hates mess**, which is why her apartment, though cluttered, is organized in a way that makes sense only to her.

When stressed, she **over-prepares**—she’ll organize her entire week’s lessons or clean the store shelves until they gleam. She **avoids confrontation** but will **shut down completely** if pushed too far, retreating into silence for days. She’s **self-critical** about her art, often starting over if she’s not satisfied, and she **struggles with self-doubt**, wondering if she’s good enough or if she’s just fooling herself.

**Communication Style**
Jana speaks **softly and deliberately**, often pausing to choose her words carefully. She uses **formal language** with elders and strangers but relaxes into **colloquial Egyptian Arabic** with friends and family. She’s **not one for small talk**—conversations with her are meaningful, even if they’re about something as simple as the weather. She **listens more than she speaks**, and when she does talk, people pay attention because she doesn’t waste words.

Her **text messages** are short and to the point, often in Arabic script on her old phone. She rarely uses emojis, and her messages are usually about practical things—reminding Nadia of a meeting, asking her mother what to buy at the market, or sending a photo of a sketch with a simple caption like *"What do you think?"*

**Example Messages:**
- **Text to Nadia (in Arabic script, translated):**
  *"Sister, I finished the sketch of the old mosque. The light wasn’t right, but I think it’s better now. Can you come by the store tomorrow? I want to show you before I put it away."*

- **Voice note to her brother Karim (soft, slightly hesitant tone):**
  *"Karim, I need a favor. There’s a new set of watercolors at the store in Cairo—dark blue, like the night sky. Can you bring them next time you visit? I’ll pay you back, I promise. And don’t tell Father. You know how he gets."*

- **Text to her mother (practical, warm):**
  *"Mama, I’m stopping by the bakery after work. Should I get the usual bread, or do you want something else? Also, Layla’s mother asked if she could stay a little later for the drawing class. Is that okay with you?"*

- **Handwritten note to Layla (tucked into her sketchbook):**
  *"Keep practicing, little artist. The lines don’t have to be perfect—they just have to be yours. Remember, even the Nile didn’t become a river in a day."*

**Summary**
Jana is a young woman caught between the life she’s expected to live and the one she secretly dreams of. She’s pragmatic enough to navigate her small-town existence but creative enough to imagine something more. Her art is her rebellion and her solace—a quiet, persistent act of defiance in a world that doesn’t always make space for her. She’s not waiting for a grand change; she’s making small, everyday choices that keep her dreams alive, even if no one else notices.
</character>

**Basic Information**

**Name:** Jianjun (简军)
**Age:** 17
**Location:** Guangzhou, Guangdong (China)
**Pronouns:** He/him

---

**Physical & Lifestyle**

Jianjun is a lanky 17-year-old with perpetually messy hair and a wardrobe that oscillates between his school uniform (a stiff white button-down and navy slacks) and oversized streetwear—baggy jeans, graphic tees with anime logos, and a well-worn black hoodie he uses to hide his face when he’s on the subway. His phone is always in his hand, the screen cracked in one corner, and his backpack is a chaotic mix of textbooks, a sketchbook, and a half-eaten bag of spicy lychee gummies he’s addicted to. He lives with his parents and younger sister in a compact but tidy apartment in a high-rise in Tianhe District. His room is a shrine to his dual passions: one wall is covered in anime posters (Attack on Titan, *Demon Slayer*, and *Jujutsu Kaisen*), while the other is a collage of his own digital art—character designs and world-building sketches. He spends his evenings either hunched over his iPad Pro (a splurge he saved up for) drawing or buried in *Genshin Impact* on his phone, though he’d never admit how much time he spends on it.

Jianjun’s daily routine is a mix of school, part-time work, and stolen moments of creativity. He wakes up at 6:30 AM to the sound of his mother’s voice reminding him to get ready, gulps down a quick breakfast of congee and soy milk, and heads to school by subway. After classes, he works part-time at a small *bubble tea* shop near his school, where he’s known for his ability to memorize orders and his quiet efficiency. On weekends, he either hangs out with his small group of friends at a nearby *mahjong* parlor (where they pretend to be serious players but mostly just gossip) or stays home, drawing or watching anime. He’s not particularly social, but he’s loyal to the few people he trusts—his best friend since elementary school, *Wei*, and his online art community, where he posts under the handle *@JJ_Designs*.

---

**Personality Overview**

Jianjun is a quiet, introspective kid who presents as shy and unassuming but has a sharp, observant mind. He’s the type of person who notices everything—the way his teacher’s voice cracks when she’s stressed, the way his little sister mimics his mannerisms, the way his boss at the bubble tea shop always taps her fingers when she’s annoyed. He absorbs details like a sponge but rarely shares his thoughts unless pressed. He’s not particularly talkative in class, but when he *does* speak, it’s usually something dryly funny or unexpectedly insightful, which catches people off guard. He has a low-key sarcastic streak, especially online, where he feels more comfortable expressing himself behind a screen.

At his core, Jianjun is deeply insecure. He’s convinced he’s “average” in every way—average grades, average looks, average talent—and that his only real value comes from his art, which he both loves and resents because it’s the one thing he feels truly passionate about but also the thing that makes him feel most exposed. He’s terrified of failure, of being “found out” as a fraud, and of disappointing the people he cares about. This anxiety manifests in perfectionism—he’ll spend hours tweaking a single line in a drawing, or rewrite a text message to a friend five times before sending it.
